nodes.name: Primordial Age
nodes.summary: Earliest age of Wraeclast: a molten world of ooze and magma inhabited by Titans, in which Kalandra found her lake. Chronology is explicitly unclear.

sources.locator: Prehistory: 'When Wraeclast was a primordial molten world of ooze and magma'

nodes.name: Precursor Era
nodes.summary: Age of the Precursor civilisation, the only culture wholly predating the Winter of the World; its apex lies further before the Vaal than the Vaal lie before the present.

chronology.relative: before the Winter of the World

nodes.name: Ancient Azmeri/Ezomyte Age
nodes.summary: Era of the primeval civilisation, Winter of the World, Lightless war and the ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui peoples, before the Eternal Empire (1 IC).

sources.locator: sections Primeval civilization, The Azmeri, The Maraketh, The Ezomytes

nodes.name: Wraeclast
nodes.summary: The continent on which the Exile's story takes place; PoE2 is set on (and expands) Wraeclast, while Oriath is another continent seen in PoE1.

nodes.name: Ngamakanui
nodes.summary: Karui homeland, an archipelago southwest of Lioneye's Watch; to the Karui the name (Nga + Makanui, 'the Karui Way') denotes anywhere the Karui roam. Explorable in PoE2 Act 4, where it is overrun by the Flesh Scourge (speculative per wiki).

nodes.name: Vastiri (Plains / Desert)
nodes.summary: Region bordering Phaaryl, Lira Vaal and Sarn, home of the Maraketh; once a lush land of forests and seven rivers around Keth, it became a desert over thousands of years after the Beast silenced the gods.

nodes.name: Keth
nodes.summary: Ancient Maraketh city and trade empire at the meeting of seven rivers, called the 'glory of the world'; ruins form an Act 2 area in PoE2.

nodes.name: Kalguur
nodes.summary: Homeland of the Kalguur people in Middengard, a distant continent southeast/east of Wraeclast; not directly accessible but referenced by Expedition and Settlers of Kalguur.

nodes.name: Middengard
nodes.summary: Distant continent east/southeast of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.

nodes.name: Ezomyr
nodes.summary: Ezomyte homeland on a landmass west of the Wraeclastian mainland (with the Isles of Skothe), later largely wiped out by a plague; Ogham forests in PoE2 Act 1.

nodes.name: Isles of Skothe
nodes.summary: Landmass west of Sarn named with Ezomyr as the origin of the Ezomytes.

nodes.name: Azmerian Ranges
nodes.summary: Mountain homeland of the ancient Azmeri; origin of the migrants who founded Sarn and the Eternal Empire, and where the Vaal first met the Azmeri.

nodes.name: Viridian Wildwood
nodes.summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons there, the Maji fight the Nameless and the King in the Mists. PoE2 Last of the Druids setting.

sources.locator: The Winter of the World > The Viridian Wildwood

nodes.name: Phrecia (imperial heartlands)
nodes.summary: Imperial heartlands of the Eternal Empire named in honour of General Alano Phrecia after he drove away a pervasive darkness; contains Phrecia Cathedral (modern Fellshrine Ruins).

nodes.name: Mount Veruso
nodes.summary: Mountain beneath which virtue gems were discovered by the Vaal, who used them to gain great power.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars that existed when 'nothing but the lake' did; Kalandra is trapped in it. The Kalandra league lets the Exile stage reflected encounters there.

nodes.name: Forge of the Titans
nodes.summary: Volcanic caldera (Crucible league) where the Molten One dwells and the Redblades worship him.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra (League)
nodes.summary: Challenge league released 19 Aug 2022 in version 3.19.0 (ended 6 Dec 2022): Mirrored Tablets let players build reflected encounters in the Lake of Kalandra.

nodes.name: Mirror of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Rarest currency item, named after Kalandra and tied to mirrored items; the PoE logo resembles it.

nodes.name: Ancient Etchings
nodes.summary: Series of etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra: her entry, view of gods as 'thieves of virtue', a conversation with a 'little thief' (Sin), the Order of the Djinn's abandoned promise, and a new escape plan.

sources.locator: Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra footnotes

nodes.name: Kalandra Trapped in the Lake
nodes.summary: Kalandra enters the primordial lake out of curiosity and can never leave: every escape returns her to the lake with no memory.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn Forsake Kalandra
nodes.summary: The Order of the Djinn swears to free Kalandra and devotes itself to her artefacts of power, but 'once they understood the truth of this place' its scribes try to erase her from history, burning their books (Kalandra page: and self-immolating out of fear); the History page words it as forsaking and abandoning her.

sources.locator: Lore > Ancient Etchings: 'burning their books and self-immolating out of fear'

nodes.name: Sin Consults Kalandra
nodes.summary: Sin seeks Kalandra at her lake and receives cryptic instructions leading him to a Precursor ruin holding the Seed of Corruption, used to create the Beast. Etching V's 'little thief' is read as Sin; PoE1 link is inference, PoE2 wiki states it directly.

nodes.name: Evilandra (Kalandra's Reflection)
nodes.summary: Rare hostile reflection of Kalandra in the Lake (game id ArbiterWildEvil) with glowing red eyes who duplicates map bosses.

nodes.name: The Titans
nodes.summary: Primordial race that walked molten Wraeclast and inhabited its volcanoes; mostly indifferent to humans; nearly wiped out in the 'rising darkness', with the Molten One the sole survivor.

nodes.name: Redblades
nodes.summary: Human tribe descended from those who settled the Titans' volcanoes; they ritually sacrifice humans to the Molten One, possibly because a Titan destroyed an outpost of El'Abin.

nodes.name: Titans and Humans Fight the Rising Darkness
nodes.summary: A 'rising darkness' (likely the Lightless after the Winter of the World) attacks Titans and humans; surviving Titans forge weapons and unearth the first virtue gem, but are almost wiped out.

nodes.name: Precursors
nodes.summary: Technologically superior ancient civilisation that wholly predates the Winter of the World; mastered corruption, built the Towers (terraforming), the Precursor Weapon and the Arbiter of Ash, then triggered cataclysms of fire, eruptions and sky-impacts. Pictographs read 'Death lies within'.

chronology.relative: further before the Vaal than the Vaal are before the present

nodes.name: Precursor Towers
nodes.summary: Precursor Tower system met on the PoE2 Atlas, apparently built for terraforming Wraeclast (per Doryani's research quoted on the History page). In Legacy of the Precursors, activating a Precursor Beacon makes a Precursor Fortress rise from the ground; the Ziggurat sits over ancient 'leylines'.

sources.locator: flavour: 'they sought to master this world'
Activate the Precursor Beacon: 'the Precursor Fortress will rise from the ground'; Doryani on leylines

nodes.name: Flame Seed
nodes.summary: Precursor object guarded by the Arbiter of Ash; very little is known.

sources.locator: Precursor civilization: 'create the Arbiter of Ash to guard the Flame Seed'

nodes.name: Arbiter of Ash
nodes.summary: Guardian created by the Precursors to guard the Flame Seed; PoE2 endgame boss.

nodes.name: Precursor Edicts
nodes.summary: Vague Precursor murals depicting the Beast and possibly instructions for containing it; Beast's origins thus pre-date the gods.

nodes.name: Precursor Cataclysm
nodes.summary: After mastering corruption the Precursors delved into world secrets, triggering great fires, eruptions and impacts from the sky; the civilisation was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm. Cause unclear.

nodes.name: Precursor Weapon
nodes.summary: Device built by the Precursors against corruption; Doryani sought to harness it (a lore video says it was scattered by 400 BIC, Doryani holding one piece and three in the Karui archipelago). In PoE2 Act 4 the Exile hunts its three pieces in Ngamakanui; in the endgame only the Hooded One is said able to wield it against the Beast.

nodes.name: The Hooded One
nodes.summary: Dark hooded god-like figure, likely Sin (PoE2 wiki inference), impaled by Count Geonor who takes the Seed of Corruption from him in PoE2's opening cinematic; in the endgame quest Legacy of the Precursors he sleeps in thrall to the Beast's corruption and is the intended wielder of the Precursor Weapon. A YouTube lore creator says Act 4 hints he was once a Precursor (community theory, unconfirmed).

nodes.name: Primeval Civilization
nodes.summary: Ancient culture (internally called 'Proto-Vaal') buried beneath Vaal and Lightless ruins in the Azurite Mines, known from glyphs; First King Uzaza, tyrant Putembo, last king Aul. No proven link to the Vaal.

nodes.name: Uzaza, the First King
nodes.summary: Founder of the primeval civilisation who led his people on a migration in a cold winter; named on Uzaza's rings.

nodes.name: Putembo
nodes.summary: Tyrant of the primeval civilisation who forced subjects to quarry stone for his fortress; overthrown by Aul.

nodes.name: Aul, the Crystal King
nodes.summary: Slave who led an uprising against Putembo, became Ahn and a tyrant, bargained with Kulemak, and as possessed golems destroyed his realm enacted a final ritual encasing his citadel in azurite crystal. Delve boss.

nodes.name: Ahkeli, the Clayshaper
nodes.summary: Primeval survivor whose home and family were destroyed, who sought refuge in the ash clouds and joined a Maraketh akhara to found the Order of the Djinn and defeat the Lightless; died before Solerai and Lundara ended the Winter.

sources.locator: Primeval civilization: Ahkeli; The Order of the Djinn

nodes.name: Aul's Uprising
nodes.summary: Aul, a slave, overthrows the tyrant Putembo and becomes the Crystal King.

nodes.name: Aul and Kulemak's Bargain
nodes.summary: Weakened Kulemak offers Aul 'untold power and mastery' for a single golem; the golem is infused with necromancy and the first Lightless/possessed golems result, ultimately toppling the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: Aul's Final Ritual
nodes.summary: In his last moments Aul rapidly crystallises his citadel with azurite, becoming the Crystal King.

sources.locator: Primeval civilization > Aul: 'In the final moments of his reign, he enacted the final ritual, encasing his palace in crystals'

nodes.name: Fall of the Primeval Civilization
nodes.summary: The primeval civilisation is toppled by possessed golems (probably the Lightless), as the Winter of the World approaches.

nodes.name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
nodes.summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.

sources.locator: The Winter of the World > The Lightless

nodes.name: Lightless Invasion
nodes.summary: After ash blocked the sun, the Lightless surface and devastate the primeval civilisation, felled Titans and the Maraketh/Azmeri cultures; a coalition under the Third Pact opposes them.

sources.locator: intro; The Winter of the World

nodes.name: Founding of the Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Ahkeli and a dekhara of surviving Maraketh found the Order, using golems and relics of power to push back the Lightless and save the Vastiri Plains.

nodes.name: Return of the Sun
nodes.summary: The Winter of the World ends: Maraketh tradition credits twin sekhema Solerai and Lundara expelling the Lightless; official Abyss text credits Solaris. Sources differ (possibly the same figures).

sources.locator: The Lightless final paragraph; The Maraketh

nodes.name: Great Wasting
nodes.summary: Karui name for the apocalyptic age of horror and famine also called the Great Fire (Ezomyte) and Winter of the World (Maraketh); Karui ancestors and Maraketh gods are said to emerge in it.

nodes.name: Great Fire
nodes.summary: Ezomyte cataclysm: the First Ones, unhonoured, spill fire out of a mountain; leaders turned to ash, survivors fed on tainted grain from Mother Gull. PoE2 reveals it is the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: Azmeri
nodes.summary: One of the oldest peoples of Wraeclast from the Azmerian Ranges; first lettered by the Vaal, worshipped Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi; their migrants founded the Eternal Empire (only pre-1 IC history counts as 'Azmerian'); Maji remnants in the Wildwood.

nodes.name: The Maji
nodes.summary: Azmeri vanguard chosen when the Wildwood was made; they purge the Nameless and fight the King in the Mists, forbidden from touching virtue gems ('Tears of the Maji').

nodes.name: The Draiocht
nodes.summary: Goddess protecting the Azmeri, divided into the Three Sisters Mhacha, Catha, Morrigan who gave themselves to imbue nature; created the Wildwood and forbade gems. Original name lost.

nodes.name: Tears of the Maji
nodes.summary: Azmeri term for virtue gems, which they are forbidden to touch; contact causes a horrific reaction.

nodes.name: The Nameless
nodes.summary: Shadowy beings born with the Wildwood as the 'unseen reflection opposite the mortal world'; led by the King in the Mists; Gruthkul was one.

nodes.name: Ezomytes
nodes.summary: People of Ezomyr and the Isles of Skothe who worship the First Ones; Ezomyr was later largely wiped by plague; speak Ezo.

nodes.name: Plague of Ezomyr
nodes.summary: At some point most of Ezomyr was wiped out by a plague (per Kahuturoa), after Oriath was recently established.

nodes.name: The Greatwolf
nodes.summary: Ezomyte First One that possessed Thane Rigwald after he sought its power in the Purity Rebellion.

nodes.name: Craiceann, First of the Deep
nodes.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the deep.

nodes.name: Farrul, First of the Plains
nodes.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the plains.

nodes.name: Fenumus, First of the Night
nodes.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the night; wove a net during the Great Fire.

nodes.name: Saqawal, First of the Sky
nodes.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the sky; stilled the Great Fire's flames.

nodes.name: Mother Gull
nodes.summary: Figure who pitied Great Fire survivors and gave them grain and water that was tainted, causing cannibalism.

nodes.name: Maraketh
nodes.summary: Matriarchal people led by sekhema, ancient dwellers of Vastiri for 304 generations; endured the Winter of the World, expelled the Lightless, had a thousand-year golden age at Keth, then lost their gods to the Beast's slumber and drifted into the desert.

nodes.name: Maraketh Golden Age
nodes.summary: Roughly a thousand years of glory after Solerai and Lundara expelled the Lightless, in a lush Vastiri of seven rivers; ended when the Beast silenced the gods.

nodes.name: Vastiri Becomes a Desert
nodes.summary: Over thousands of years the plains' rivers dried and forests became sand, naturally or via Maraketh/Halani-linked causes; the Maraketh became semi-nomadic.

nodes.name: Afarud
nodes.summary: Outcasts of the Faridun who use forbidden rites and seek destruction of Maraketh and Faridun alike, led by Saresh.

nodes.name: Saresh
nodes.summary: Faridun reject and necromancer of Weeping Black, former Order of the Djinn member; defeated by Garukhan (Orbala) with the Horn of the Vastiri.

nodes.name: Sekhema
nodes.summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.

nodes.name: Karui
nodes.summary: Nomadic seafaring people of Ngamakanui following the Karui Way; once peaceful farmers and fishermen until Tukohama armed them; ever-changing pantheon; Hinekora made the Halls of the Dead.

nodes.name: Karui Way (Makanui)
nodes.summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.

nodes.name: Kalguuran Expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm's omens, King Cadigan III sends an expedition with the Triskelion Flame led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved; they colonise Vaal ruins, until horrors, a priesthood plot and the loss of the Flame destroy the colony.

nodes.name: King Cadigan the Third
nodes.summary: Kalguuran king who commissioned the expedition and banned gems after Azmeri panic over gem drawings.

nodes.name: Olroth
nodes.summary: Knights of the Sun leader, 'the Gallant' then 'the Grim'; staked the Triskelion Flame, defeated the Empty-Eyed Fiend with a gem, was stabbed by priests; now boss Olroth, Origin of the Fall.

nodes.name: Uhtred
nodes.summary: High Priest of the Order of the Chalice who disliked gems, plotted against Olroth and fled to the Precursor Shrine; now Uhtred, Covetous Traitor.

nodes.name: Vorana
nodes.summary: Black Scythes mercenary leader who took up gems and fought on; later Vorana, Last to Fall.

nodes.name: Medved
nodes.summary: Druid of the Broken Circle who discovered soul vapour leaving corpses toward gems; became a horror champion, Medved, Feller of Heroes.

nodes.name: Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: Sacred flame whose starlight barrier protected the Kalguuran colony; destroyed by the Exile in the Olroth fight.

nodes.name: Precursor Shrine
nodes.summary: Underground shrine built around a mirror by the 'oldest of men' (probably primeval/precursor); Uhtred hid here and the Kalguuran survivors tried to reach it. No link to Kalandra's mirror is proven.

nodes.name: Knights of the Sun
nodes.summary: Kalguuran martial order led by Olroth who adopted gems on weapons and armour.

nodes.name: Black Scythes
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries led by Vorana, fighting horrors from walls with crossbows.

nodes.name: Order of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Kalguuran priesthood led by Uhtred; found the ancient artefact at the shrine.

nodes.name: Druids of the Broken Circle
nodes.summary: Kalguuran nature-mystics under Medved, named after Olroth's gem use clouded their scrying.

nodes.name: Empty-Eyed Fiend
nodes.summary: Horror Olroth could not harm with mortal blade or flame until a gem's starlight beheaded it.

nodes.name: Perpetual Night over the Imperial Heartlands
nodes.summary: Azmerian writers describe part of the empire cast into perpetual night, a 'dark being' dismembering Emperor Caspiro, until General Alano Phrecia dispelled it, 'returning the gaze of Solaris'. Likely the darkness later sealed in the Oversoul (per GGG Q&A).

chronology.relative: Caspiro died ~5 years after Veruso; Alano Phrecia quote dated first Sacrato of Lurici, 35 IC

sources.locator: Alano Phrecia quote: '... our legions drove the dark being deep into the recesses of its lair and sealed it away for eternity' (35 IC)

nodes.name: Legacy of Phrecia
nodes.summary: 'Legacy of Phrecia': a limited returning PoE1 event (ascendancy/idol rework). First run ended 23 Apr 2025; it returned during the 3.27 (Keepers of the Flame) cycle from 29 Jan 2026 for about 20 days, per third-party news. Its lore link to the ancient Phrecian/imperial-heartland history is by name only (unverified).

chronology.relative: first run ended Apr 2025; 3.27-cycle rerun 29 Jan - 19 Feb 2026 (third-party news)

sources.locator: article on the end of the event (23 Apr 2025)
official event page (not re-fetched by checker)

nodes.name: Imperial Seven-Day Week
nodes.summary: Eternal seven-day week named after components of existence: Solaro, Lunaro, Fiero, Glacio, Galvano, Kaso, Sacrato.

nodes.name: Thirteen Moons
nodes.summary: Thirteen Imperial months (Verusi, Divini, Derivi, Phreci, Caspiri, Astrali, Eterni, Atziri, Vivici, Lurici, Sagari, Vitali, Azmeri), some named for renowned figures; Wraeclast has seasons.

nodes.name: Before Imperial Calendar (BIC)
nodes.summary: Dating convention for events preceding Imperial year 1 (e.g. Vaal fall c. 400 BIC; Vaal–Azmeri contact c. 1200 BIC).

sources.locator: The Vaal > Contacting the Azmeri; The End of Vaal Civilization (c. 400 BIC)

nodes.name: Act 4 (PoE2)
nodes.summary: PoE2's fourth act, set in the Karui archipelago of Ngamakanui, where the player searches for three pieces of the Precursor Weapon (and a way to assemble it) to subdue the Beast.

nodes.name: Aul's Domain (Crystal King's Throne)
nodes.summary: Delve area (internally 'Proto-Vaal city') of the Azurite Mine where the crystal-encased citadel and throne of Aul, the Crystal King, lie.

sources.locator: Primeval civilization; footnote: 'Proto-Vaal' is the internal name of Delve's Primeval Chamber and The Crystal King's Throne

nodes.name: The Caaltu
nodes.summary: A civilisation that existed in Kahuturoa's time (Vastiri still forest, Vaal extant, Oriath recently founded, Ezomyr not yet struck by plague) and was only a memory by Maata's time. Little else is known.
